messages:
anya: FYI ran microbench after the kernel-selector change (PR #4321) and I see TP all-reduce tail latency jump for large reduces on the 8-way TP cluster. Uploading traces and bench summary.

kevin: can you drop the bench invocation & raw numbers?

anya: bench command:
```
./tp_allreduce_bench --topology=8tp --msg-sizes=32k,128k,256k,512k,1m --reps=300 --kv-cache=on --kernels=quant+fused
```
median results (local dev-cluster):
- 32KB   ring=0.7ms  tree=0.8ms
- 128KB  ring=1.4ms  tree=1.3ms
- 256KB  ring=3.2ms  tree=1.7ms
- 512KB  ring=5.5ms  tree=2.0ms
- 1MB    ring=9.0ms  tree=2.5ms
p99 end-to-end generation increased from ~20ms -> ~29ms on traces with long prompts.
perf artifacts: https://ci.internal/bench/20411 (nvprof + ethtool counters)

dev-bench-bot: perf run uploaded: https://ci.internal/bench/20411

maria: that 256KB+ gap is scary. did the selector change alter fragment size or packing rules?

anya: yes, selector prefers fused attention kernel which emits larger contiguous reduce payloads (less internal fragmentation). previously we split attention outputs into ~128KB fragments. now those fragments are bigger.

samir: two things to consider: (1) ring path seems to suffer when messages cross a network buffer threshold -> backpressure/pipeline stalls; (2) KV cache packing might create non-aligned sizes causing suboptimal channelization in NCCL.

oliver: quick test idea: force NCCL_ALGO=tree and NCCL_BUFFSIZE=262144 and rerun.

kevin: did that. with NCCL_ALGO=tree 1MB drops from 9.0ms -> 2.6ms; p99 back to baseline. But tree has different saturation behavior at high concurrency. We need scale results.

maria: ok, so immediate mitigations: a) revert the selector change b) make selector keep chunk sizes < threshold c) prefer tree for certain msg size ranges. pros/cons?

anya: I attached nvprof flame showing ~1.4ms kernel stall waiting on allreduce for the 1MB case. stack shows lots of small cudaMemcpy calls queued while GPU waits.

samir: I also looked at NIC counters from ethtool in the uploaded artifact. On the problematic runs we see high tx_queue_drops and increased retries when msg > 256KB. Possibly NIC driver or switch buffering interaction.

kevin: experiment: padded payloads to next 512KB boundary and reran ring. 1MB reduced from 9.0ms -> 3.3ms. So making sizes aligned helps the ring algorithm.

oliver: interesting — padding trades bytes for latency. need cost model for bytes transferred vs latency improvement. Also NCCL internal chunking (NCCL_BUFFSIZE) matters. when NCCL_BUFFSIZE=128KB the ring stalls less for some cases.

maria: action items:
- kevin: run scale matrix (8/16/32 TP) with forced tree, ring+padding, ring+small-chunks; collect NIC counters + nvlink stats. due EOD tomorrow.
- samir: bisect PR #4321 and isolate the line that changed fragmentation boundary. propose patch to optionally emit smaller reduces.
- anya: reproduce with kv-cache disabled to see amplification effect; attach end-to-end traces.
- oliver: prototype runtime heuristic: prefer tree when msg_size > 220KB on cross-node topologies; test impact on throughput.

kevin: I started 16/32 TP runs. initial 16TP results: tree keeps latency ~baseline; ring w/o padding regresses; ring+padded gets close to tree but uses ~6-8% more network bytes.

samir: if KV-cache growth is the amplifier, maybe we can keep fused kernel but add split-emit stage for large tensors to produce safe reduce sizes for ring. less invasive than revert.

anya: good point. also note production only sees this in long prompt tails where many cached KV blocks cause consecutive large reduces; short requests unaffected.

oliver: I'll draft the heuristic and simulate decision boundaries using kevin's numbers. need a perf matrix to pick threshold and fallback rules.

maria: coordinate with infra if we go down the NIC tuning path (ethtool sysctl, driver knobs). This could have cluster-wide impact.

dev-bench-bot: Created issue INF-8721: "tp-allreduce: kernel selector vs message size interaction causing ring tail latencies" https://tracker.internal/INF-8721

anya: I'll open RFC with attached artifacts and 3 remediation PRs (revert, split-emitter, runtime-heuristic). For now hold rolling selector to prod.

kevin: posting raw CSV and ethtool dumps once all runs complete.

samir: ping me if you want help bisecting the selector. I'm available to pair with the author.

maria: thanks everyone. keep logs here and paste short summary when done. :thumbsup:
